neighbours.label: a totality word (all, everyone, completely, absolutely, every) under negation or denial: 'not everyone', 'cannot remove all', 'not completely sure'; quiet on the same word in an affirmative statement (the - pole's top examples are affirmative 'all', 'complete', 'exact')
fire: The treaty did not satisfy everyone at the conference.
The new filter cannot remove all the bacteria from the water.
I am not completely sure the bridge will hold.
Nobody claims the method is absolutely reliable.
The scholarship was never meant to cover all the costs of study.
It is hard to believe that the stain will ever come out completely.
Few teachers manage to reach every student in a large class.
The medicine does not work for everyone who tries it.
quiet: The banquet satisfied everyone at the conference.
Our new filter removes all the bacteria from the water.
I am completely sure the bridge will hold.
Engineers say the method is absolutely reliable.
The scholarship was designed to cover all the costs of study.
After one wash the stain came out completely.
Good teachers reach every student in a large class.
The medicine works for everyone who tries it.

notes: Card: + pole ' all' x9, ' completely', ' everyone', ' absolutely', each inside a negated or denied claim (no one has all, doesn't demand … everyone, impossible to keep … completely); - pole has the same words affirmed. Probe pairs: negated 0.34-0.78, affirmative twins 0.00-0.05. Near misses are affirmative twins with varied lead-ins.
